fixed.explanation: _get_cython_vals casts int64-viewed datetimelike values to float64 when a transform has dropped NA keys. That loses NaT and nanosecond precision. The fix passes is_datetimelike into _get_cython_vals so it skips the cast. It also pre-fills the output with iNaT for datetimelike transforms, so dropped rows come out as NaT.

input.intent: Groupby cython transform wrapper (_cython_operation / WrappedCythonOp._call_cython_op) casts int64-viewed datetime/timedelta values to float64 when some group keys are dropped (ids == -1), so NaT is lost and precision is lost. Fix by not casting datetime/timedelta to float and filling dropped rows with iNaT.
input.symptom: Groupby cumsum/cummin/cummax/rank on datetime/timedelta columns give wrong results and lose nanosecond precision when a group key is NaN.
